===Etymology 1===
[[File:Dubrovnik-port.jpg|right|thumb|The old port of [[Dubrovnik]]]]
{{etymon|en|id=portus|:inh|ang:port<id:portus>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|ang|port}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|portus||port, harbour}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*pértus||crossing}} (and thus a distant doublet of {{doublet|notext=1|en|ford}}). The directional sense, attested since at least the 1500s, derives from ancient vessels with the steering oar on the right (see etymology of [[starboard]]), which therefore had to moor with their left sides facing the dock or wharf. {{doublet|en|fjard|fjord|firth|ford|Portus}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}
{{wp|[[+|+ (place where ships dock)]]}}

# {{senseid|en|harbour}} {{topics|en|Ports and harbours}} A place on the [[coast]] at which ships can [[shelter]], or [[dock]] to load and unload [[cargo]] or [[passenger]]s.
#: {{syn|en|harbour|haven}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|1|1|passage=peering in maps for '''ports''' and piers and roads}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-08|volume=407|issue=8839|page=52|magazine=w:The Economist
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/international/21579039-chinas-growing-empire-ports-abroad-mainly-about-trade-not-aggression-new-masters The new masters and commanders]
|passage=From the ground, Colombo's '''port''' does not look like much. Those entering it are greeted by wire fences, walls dating back to colonial times and security posts. For mariners leaving the '''port''' after lonely nights on the high seas, the delights of the B52 Night Club and Stallion Pub lie a stumble away.}}
# {{senseid|en|port city}} A town or city containing such a place, a [[port city]].
#: {{syn|en|[[harbour]] [[city]]|[[harbour]] [[town]]|port city}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|author=Mark Townsend|title=‘We are seen as less human’: inside Marseille’s districts abandoned by the police|work=The Observer|date=2023-07-01|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2023/jul/01/we-are-seen-as-less-human-inside-marseilles-quartiers-that-the-police-have-abandoned|issn=0029-7712|passage=More broadly, the '''port''' is seen as a litmus test for France; if its most multicultural city can foster vast Muslim enclaves viewed with broad suspicion or hostility by the police, then what hope is there elsewhere?}}
# {{lb|en|nautical|aviation|uncountable}} The left-hand side of a [[vessel]], including aircraft, when one is facing forward. Used to unambiguously refer to directions relative to the vessel structure, rather than to a person or object on board.

#: {{ant|en|starboard}}
# {{lb|en|rowing}} A [[sweep]] [[rower]] that primarily rows with an oar on the port side.
#: {{ux|en|Each eight has four '''ports''' and four starboards.}}
